title: The results contract can carry a value that is settled, conditional or withheld: version 1.3.0, strictly additive, with its runtime copy, generated types and one contract test; nothing emits it yet (work order Part 0, decision D5; D-090 R229, R255, R258, R268)
objective: Make the results contract able to say, for ONE value inside an answer, which of the three ways of the work order it appears in (docs/plans/R6B_RESULTS_CONNECTION_WORK_ORDER_2026-10-06.md, section 0 'How a result may appear', section 4 item 4, section 7 decision D5, section 10): settled (the number, its law section, its sources), conditional ('If <the assumption>: <the number>', naming each assumption, its kind and what would settle it) or withheld ('not known', the reason, what would resolve it, and whether it is missing information or work still owed; never a number, never a zero). Today a value must be a number and only a whole answer can be 'not available', so coverage cannot read 'not known' beside heights that are shown. THE ORCHESTRATOR'S DECISION ON D5 (the work order's recommendation): a new contract version, 1.3.0, added in the same way versions 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 were added: STRICTLY ADDITIVE. Required properties of the design: (a) every document that is valid today stays valid byte for byte, and every fixture that is invalid today stays invalid; (b) the new fields are optional in the schema and a document that carries any of them declares 1.3.0 (a version-binding rule like the two existing ones); (c) in a document that declares 1.3.0 every value of every available answer states its way: none is settled by silence; (d) a value that is shown (settled or conditional) keeps the present value object and its number; a conditional value carries at least one condition with its kind (a user's statement about the lot; a recorded figure that another figure contradicts; a condition that was not checked and is assumed not to apply), the assumption in words and what would settle it; a settled value carries no condition; (e) a withheld value carries NO number: it is listed beside the shown values of the same answer with its key, its label, the reason, the kind (missing information for this property, or work the program still owes), what would resolve it and, where one applies, the law section; the same key is never both shown and withheld in one answer; (f) the whole-answer 'not available' object may say, in 1.3.0, what would resolve it and which of the two kinds it is, without changing its present required fields; (g) nothing about the remaining-floor-area line changes (its wording is settled by the owner); (h) the existing type of a shown value's number stays a number in the generated types, so no present reader of a results document has to change. The builder may choose the field names and the exact shape inside these properties, and says in its report what it chose and why. Then: the runtime copy of the schema is re-synced and the generated types are regenerated, each with its script; one new contract test file proves the properties above with documents built in the test (valid: one answer with shown heights and a withheld coverage; a conditional floor area naming a contradicted recorded figure and an unchecked condition; a withheld unit limit that is missing information; invalid: a conditional value without a condition, a settled value with one, a withheld value carrying a number, a key both shown and withheld, a 1.3.0 document with a value that states no way, the new fields under a lower version). NOTHING EMITS 1.3.0 IN THIS TASK: no engine, route, screen, drawing or saved result changes, and NO new file is added under packages/contracts/fixtures/valid/results/ (the drawing and CAD snapshot suites read every file there).
business_reason: Part 0 of the work order cannot make a result honest while the contract can only carry a number or drop a whole answer. With the contract merged first and nothing using it, the engine and the website can then be built at the same time by different builders without writing the same file. The owner's rules: unknown information stays unknown (R229); a user's assumption supports only a clearly labelled conditional result (R255); missing information and unfinished work are different (R258); for unchecked conditions, unaffected answers stay visible, defensible assumptions are labelled conditional and only what cannot be supported is withheld (R268).

scope_corrections.change: [ORCH-CORRECTED 2026-10-07, after the builder's work and the independent data-contract review, before submit] The packet's properties (c) (in a 1.3.0 document no value is settled by silence) and (e) (the same key is never both shown and withheld), and scenarios S5 and S7, presumed that a JSON schema can enforce both in full. The independent reviewer showed with its own documents that it cannot: JSON Schema 2020-12 has no way to compare the keys of the items of the values list with the property names of a sibling object, in this shape or any other. What the schema does enforce stays required: a way entry that states no way is refused; an available answer of a 1.3.0 document without way entries is refused; a withheld entry with a number is refused; one entry mixing two ways is refused. The two cross-list rules stay requirements of the work order's Part 0 as a whole: they are owed to the validator of the engine that first emits 1.3.0 and are recorded as backlog row DB-171, to be bound into that task's packet. In this task they are pinned by tests that fail the day the gap is closed. Scenario S5 'expected' was: 'rejected'. Scenario S7 'expected' was: 'each rejected'. Both now say exactly what is refused by the schema and what is owed. No path, gate, reviewer or other scenario changed. The reviewer's ruling: these cannot be met inside the task's allowed paths, and need not be closed in this task while nothing emits 1.3.0.
